about:
The Georgia Electronic Design Center (GEDC) operates from Atlanta, Georgia, as part of the Georgia Institute of Technology. The center does not disclose a founding year or private ownership structure; it functions as a university-based research institute focused on electronics and photonics.

GEDC integrates electronics, photonics, and artificial intelligence/machine learning to advance high-speed components and system performance. Its core activities include multi-principal investigator sponsored research, industry engagement programs, and foundry access for prototyping. The center hosts more than 15 active faculty members and over 100 graduate and undergraduate students, making it one of the largest university-based semiconductor research centers in the world. Partners may establish design centers in Technology Square or within GEDC facilities to collaborate directly with researchers on directed projects.

The center serves industry partners across sectors that require high-speed electronic and photonic innovation, including semiconductor, telecommunications, and advanced computing. Companies engage through sponsored research agreements, consortium memberships, and direct collaboration with faculty and students to commercialize emerging technologies.

GEDC’s stated mission is to accelerate commercialization by transferring faculty and student innovations to industry through strong partnerships and consortia. It aims to empower partners to become technology leaders by providing prompt access to research breakthroughs and collaborative design infrastructure.
